``` {r scores and rankings}
# top 5 highest and lowest countries per category(life expectancy, GDP, ) per year (2000 & 2015?). standardise by population? -> make new df with standardised per category of interest. or is it already standardised? check WHO
#maybe take the top 5 from 2000, follow them over the years?
#applied piping like we learned. any other new techniques?

class(Life_Expectancy_Data)
  
high5<- Life_Expectancy_Data %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  slice_max(Life_expectancy, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
high5

high5_2000 <- filter(high5, Year==2000)

low5<- Life_Expectancy_Data %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  slice_min(Life_expectancy, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

low5_2000 <- filter(low5, Year==2000)

#Is de life expectancy/adult mortality/GDP/etc in developing countries over de jaren toegenomen/afgenomen?
 #use ggalluvial?
library(ggplot2)
data <- Life_Expectancy_Data
ggplot(data,
       aes(x=Year, stratum = Region, Alluvium= Country,
       y= Life_expectancy))+
   scale_x_discrete(expand = c(.1, .1)) +
  geom_text(stat = "alluvium", size = 3) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("test")
 
data_test <- data
class(data_test)
# filter developing countries, group per year. then focus on each categopry (GDP, adult mortality, life expectancy) over the years
data_test <- as.tibble (data_test)
class(data_test)
data_test %<>% select(Country, Region, Year, Adult_mortality, GDP_per_capita, Life_expectancy)
    

data_ME <- data_test %>% filter (Region == "Middle East")
data_ME

install.packages("rstatix")
library(rstatix)
mean(data_ME$Adult_mortality)
mean(data_ME$GDP_per_capita[data_ME$Year==2000])

country_sets <- data_ME %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(countries = list(sort(unique(Country))))

n_distinct(country_sets$countries) # every year has same countries so repeated measures test?
library(rstatix)
library(ggrepel) #use this to add in non-overlapping country lables
pointsToLabel <- c("Russia", "Venezuela", "Iraq", "Myanmar", "Sudan",
                   "Afghanistan", "Congo", "Greece", "Argentina", "Brazil",
                   "India", "Italy", "China", "South Africa", "Spane",
                   "Botswana", "Cape Verde", "Bhutan", "Rwanda", "France",
                   "United States", "Germany", "Britain", "Barbados", "Norway", "Japan",
                   "New Zealand", "Singapore", "Netherlands")

ggplot(data_ME, aes(Year, GDP_per_capita, group = Country)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               colour = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
               colour = "red", size = 3)+
  geom_text_repel( data = filter(data_ME, Country %in% data_ME$Country),
                   aes(label = Country),
                   color = "gray20")
```

```{r}
#boxplots of the categories on the x-axis grouped together per year (2000 & 2015) - maybe diff coloured background for years?. Y axis change (difference) between 2000 and 2015, might have to do percentage 
#scatterplot to plot change per country, could colour regions differently, again percentages of change?
diff <- data %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>%
  arrange(Country, Year) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>%                       # keep countries with both years, not ones with missing values if any
  summarise(across(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy),
                   ~ (last(.x) - first(.x)) / first(.x) * 100)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Country, names_to = "variable", values_to = "diff")
diff

ggplot(diff, aes(x = variable, y = diff)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)")

ggplot(diff, aes(x = variable, y = diff)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)") #to seperate them and give their own axes, help with the different scales

data %>% filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>% group_by(Country) %>% summarise(n = n_distinct(Economy_status_Developed)) %>% filter(n > 1) #to check if every country stays in the same category

diff.dev <- data %>%. #only developing
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>%
  arrange(Country, Year) %>%
  group_by(Country, Economy_status_Developing) %>%             # keep status in the output
  filter(n() == 2) %>%
  summarise(across(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy),
                   ~ (last(.x) - first(.x)) / first(.x) * 100),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "diff.dev")

ggplot(diff.dev, aes(x = variable, y = diff.dev, fill = Economy_status_Developing)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)")
ggplot(diff.dev, aes(x = Economy_status_Developing, y = diff.dev, fill = Economy_status_Developing)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


diff.both <- data %>% #both developed and developing
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>%
  arrange(Country, Year) %>%
  group_by(Country, Economy_status_Developed) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>%
  summarise(across(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy), # why is gdp in the 100s instead of 1-100%
                   ~ (last(.x) - first(.x)) / first(.x) * 100),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Economy = factor(Economy_status_Developed,
                          levels = c(0, 1),
                          labels = c("Developing", "Developed"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "diff.both")

ggplot(diff.both, aes(x = variable, y = diff.both, fill = Economy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)", fill = NULL)

ggplot(diff.both, aes(x = Economy, y = diff.both, fill = Economy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from 2000 to 2015 (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
# can be turned into shiny if we want. example: runExample("04_mpg")   

data %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>%
  select(Country, Year, GDP_per_capita) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = GDP_per_capita) %>% # to find outlier nearing 1000% -> Eritrea
  mutate(diff.both = (`2015` - `2000`) / `2000` * 100) %>%         #Eritrea 828 to 9011, next highest is Myanmar
  arrange(desc(diff.both)) %>%                                       # Myanmar 310 to 1197 -> 286%  weird jump
  head(10)

diff.per.region <- data %>% #both developed and developing
  filter(Year %in% c(2000, 2015)) %>%
  arrange(Country, Year) %>%
  group_by(Country, Economy_status_Developed, Region) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>%
  summarise(across(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy), 
                   ~ (last(.x) - first(.x)) / first(.x) * 100),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Economy = factor(Economy_status_Developed,
                          levels = c(0, 1),
                          labels = c("Developing", "Developed"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(GDP_per_capita, Adult_mortality, Life_expectancy),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "diff.both")
diff.per.region

```
